verdict.rationale: Notte documents a live `observe()` primitive that returns element IDs and selectors for interaction, and it markets selector-free, natural-language task execution ("No selectors, no maintenance"). Explicit act/click/type primitives on described elements are not documented, and resilience to layout changes rests only on a marketing claim. Missing for 10: documented act/click/type APIs targeting described elements, evidence that actions survive selector or layout changes, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drive the page through DOM-understanding action primitives (act/click/type on described elements) that survive selector and layout changes

citations.quote: Element IDs, selectors, and field mappings must come from a live `observe()` call, CLI `notte page observe` output, or generated workflow code.
Describe a task. Watch it happen. One prompt. No selectors, no maintenance.
Give AI agents natural language tasks to complete on websites
